headline: BANNERMAN AND CNNC PULL THE TRIGGER — $353M Etango Uranium Mine in Namibia Gets Construction Green Light, 3.5M Lbs/Year Target
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX/NSX: BMN) and its Chinese partner CNNC Overseas have approved construction of the Etango uranium project in Namibia, committing to a $353 million development that targets annual output of approximately 3.5 million pounds of uranium oxide with first production in 2028. The Final Investment Decision (FID) makes Etango one of the first major new uranium mines globally to reach construction approval in the current price cycle, with long-term uranium sitting above $90/lb.

headline: NEWMONT BEATS Q3 — Then Falls 4.6%. Why Gold Miners Are Getting Sold Even When Profits Hit Records
snippet: Investor Ideas examines the counterintuitive dynamic playing out across gold producers today: Newmont reported record third-quarter profits driven by gold near $4,000/oz, yet fell 4.6% on the day — illustrating the sector-wide disconnect where even strong fundamental results can't overcome macro-driven selling pressure and institutional deleveraging. The piece identifies multiple factors including ETF redemptions, rising real yields, and gold's own correction as reasons the market is using earnings beats as exit liquidity.

headline: GOLDSEEK HUBBARTT: GOLD STOCKS NEAR A 'FINAL LOW' — Technical Patterns Suggest Sector Base Is Forming After Brutal Selloff
snippet: Morris Hubbartt's October 27 technical analysis on GoldSeek argues gold stocks are approaching a 'final low' formation, citing key indicator alignments and pattern recognition from comparable prior bottoms in the mining sector. Published today as gold hovers around $4,000 and miner indices trade 30–40% below their 2026 highs, the piece provides specific chart levels and signals that Hubbartt says would confirm the sector base is in place.

headline: JUST 7% OF URANIUM DELIVERED TO U.S. REACTORS LAST YEAR WAS DOMESTIC — Reactor Pipeline Still Expanding as Import Reliance Deepens
snippet: A data release published October 26 shows that only 7% of the uranium delivered to U.S. nuclear reactors in 2025 originated from domestic sources — the lowest share on record — even as the new reactor pipeline continues to grow with AI data centre power commitments driving re-ratings of existing and planned nuclear capacity. The statistic underscores the strategic case for U.S. uranium producers and sets the backdrop for ongoing Congressional pressure to boost domestic enrichment and mining capacity.

headline: USA RARE EARTH INITIATED AT BUY, $28 TARGET — Texas Capital Calls It 'Well-Aligned with Domestic Onshoring Tailwinds'
snippet: Texas Capital Securities initiated coverage of USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) with a Buy rating and a $28 price target, describing the company as 'well-aligned with domestic onshoring tailwinds' as Washington accelerates efforts to build a non-Chinese rare earth supply chain. USA Rare Earth is developing the Round Top heavy rare earth and critical minerals deposit in West Texas, one of the few U.S. projects with near-term production potential in heavy rare earth elements.

headline: AUSTRALIA CLEARS CHINESE TAKEOVER OF ATLANTIC LITHIUM — FIRB Approves Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt Acquisition
snippet: Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) has approved the acquisition of Atlantic Lithium (AIM/ASX: ALL) by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, a major Chinese battery materials processor, clearing the key regulatory hurdle for a deal that gives Huayou a strategic stake in the Ewoyaa lithium project in Ghana. The FIRB approval was noted in SP Angel's October 27 market view, with the acquisition now moving toward completion.

headline: KOPERNIK: GOLD AT $4,000 VS. $3,000 INCENTIVE PRICE — Why Record Miner Profits Don't Automatically Create Stock Gains
snippet: Kopernik's October analysis frames the current mining stock paradox through its 'incentive price' concept: with gold near $4,000/oz and the estimated incentive price (the level needed to justify a new mine build) at roughly $3,000/oz, the gap signals that existing producers are generating supernormal profits — yet the market is not re-rating them higher. Kopernik argues this disconnect creates the opportunity, but only for investors who understand why the gap persists and what would close it.

headline: CRITICAL METALS / EUROPEAN LITHIUM MERGER GETS WESTERN AUSTRALIA COURT STAMP — Deal Now Cleared to Complete
snippet: The Supreme Court of Western Australia has approved Critical Metals Corp's acquisition of European Lithium (ASX: EUR), which holds the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria — one of the most advanced hard-rock lithium development projects in Europe. The court order, issued October 26, follows securityholder approval on October 22 and clears the path to transaction completion, consolidating a strategically located European lithium asset under North American ownership.

headline: INDONESIA NICKEL CUTS ARE COMING — Morowali Industrial Park Operators Set to Coordinate Output Reductions as Chinese NPI Producers Plan Steep Rollbacks
snippet: Nickel Industries (ASX: NIC) has confirmed that producers in Indonesia's Morowali Industrial Park will coordinate output cuts, with Chinese operators weighing steep reductions as the nickel surplus and sub-$16,000/t prices make marginal production uneconomical. The coordinated cut, if implemented at scale, would be one of the largest supply responses in the nickel market since Indonesia imposed its ore export ban in 2020 and could materially shift the global nickel balance heading into 2027.

headline: MAGNA MINING APPROVES $70M LEVACK RESTART — Sudbury Nickel-Copper Mine Returns to Production Under Junior Operator
snippet: Magna Mining has approved a $70-million capital program to restart its Levack nickel-copper mine near Sudbury, Ontario — the former Falconbridge operation acquired from Glencore. The construction decision makes Magna one of the few junior miners globally committing new capital to nickel production during the current nickel price downturn, betting that the Indonesia output cuts will restore the market to balance before the mine reaches steady-state production.

headline: US-BACKED ORION CMC NEAR FINISH LINE ON GLENCORE CONGO COPPER-COBALT STAKES — 'Final Phases' of Dealmaking
snippet: A U.S. government-backed consortium, Orion CMC, is in the 'final phases' of completing its purchase of stakes in Glencore's copper-cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo, per a Bloomberg report from October 23. The deal is part of Washington's strategic push to secure non-Chinese access to DRC copper and cobalt as the U.S. competes with Beijing's dominant position in Central African battery metal supply chains.

headline: COBALT SPOT SLUMPS TO $15.70/LB — Cobalt Blue Bucks the Trend, Secures Swiss Metals Trader Offtake Deal
snippet: Cobalt spot prices fell to US$15.70/lb in late October 2026, down from US$18.20/lb just one month earlier, as collapsing DRC production costs and weak EV demand continue to weigh on the market. Against that backdrop, Cobalt Blue (ASX: COB) secured an early offtake agreement with a Swiss metals trading house for production from its Thackaringa cobalt project in New South Wales — a notable financing signal for a development-stage asset in a depressed market.
